artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>3$ be a prime. Denote by $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ the Legendre/Jacobi symbol, and let $B_n(x)$ denote the Bernoulli polynomial of degree $n$. Prove or disprove the following three statements.

(i) The congruence
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}}{(-48)^{3k}}\equiv\begin{cases} x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}, & \text{if }\left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{41}\right)=1\text{ and }4p=x^2+123y^2,\\[4pt] 2p-3x^2\pmod{p^2}, & \text{if }\left(\tfrac{p}{3}\right)=\left(\tfrac{p}{41}\right)=-1\text{ and }4p=3x^2+41y^2,\\[4pt] 0\pmod{p^2}, & \text{if }\left(\tfrac{p}{123}\right)=-1, \end{cases}$$
holds, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z$ in the first two cases.

(ii) For every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{615k+53}{(-48)^{3k}}\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}\equiv 53\,(p^a)+(p^{a-1})\cdot\tfrac{5}{12}\,p^2 B_{p-2}(\tfrac{1}{18})\pmod{p^3}.$$

(iii) For every integer $n\ge 2$, the rational number
$$a_n:=\frac{1}{n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(615k+53)\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}(-48)^{3(n-1-k)}$$
is an integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n$ is an integer not divisible by $3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a direct proof or disproof of this specific conjecture (involving $\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}/(-48)^{3k}$ with the discriminant $-123$). Related conjectures of Z.-W. Sun on supercongruences and divisibility of binomial sums have been proved (e.g., Guo–Liu, Mao–Sun), but no source found explicitly settles all three parts of this conjecture.
